sentiment.rationale: The document reports strong comparable sales growth of 8.9% on top of record growth last year, and EPS growth of 8.9% GAAP. Forward guidance is raised: the company now expects high single digit comparable sales growth in the second half (near the high end of previous guidance) and an operating income margin rate of 8% or higher for the full year. Management expresses confidence in the back half, stating they are 'well-positioned to deliver outstanding performance.' The score is capped at 0.30 because the guidance raise is modest (from a range to near the high end) and the margin guidance is a floor, not a specific raise, so the shift is meaningful but not dramatic.

summary.revenue: Total revenue of $25.2 billion grew 9.5% compared with last year, driven by total sales growth of 9.4% and a 20.0% increase in other revenue.
summary.eps: Second quarter GAAP EPS of $3.65 was 8.9% higher than last year, and Adjusted EPS of $3.64 was 7.9% higher than last year.
summary.guidance: For the second half of 2021, the Company expects high single digit growth in comparable sales, near the high end of the previous guidance range. The Company now expects its full year operating income margin rate will be 8 percent or higher.
summary.margin: Second quarter operating income margin rate was 9.8% in 2021 compared with 10.0% in 2020. Second quarter gross margin rate was 30.4%, compared with 30.9% in 2020.
key_risks: Higher merchandise and freight costs pressuring gross margin rate.
Comparison over last year's change in the sales return reserve estimate.
Expense rate increases to normalized levels in various expense categories, such as marketing.
key_opportunities: Benefit of low markdowns, favorable category mix, and a shift in fulfillment mix into lower-cost same-day fulfillment options.
Digital comparable sales grew 10%, led by same-day services (Order Pickup, Drive Up and Shipt) which grew nearly 55%.
More than 95% of Target’s second quarter sales were fulfilled by its stores, highlighting operational efficiency.
New $15 billion share repurchase program reflecting confidence in sustained strong performance.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: CEO Brian Cornell said, 'Even after unprecedented growth over the last two years, we see much more opportunity ahead of us, and we’re leaning into opportunities to invest in the long-term growth and resiliency of our business. ... we’re well-positioned to deliver outstanding performance in the back half of the year.'
